overviewParagraphs: Phokeethra Country Club carries the prestigious distinction of having hosted the Asian Tour's Cambodian Open — an accolade that certifies the course to a professional tournament standard and makes it one of the most credentialled layouts in Cambodia. The Asian Tour brings the world's top emerging professionals together for a serious championship test, and Phokeethra met that standard convincingly during its time as the national Open host.

The course's signature challenge is its system of forced water carries — genuine carry requirements off tees and into greens that leave no room for the layup approach that more forgiving designs allow. The water is positioned to punish truly errant shots decisively while still rewarding conservative but accurate target-finding. It is a more demanding playing experience than either Angkor Golf Resort or the Chhun On courses, and is best suited to golfers who want a genuine championship test alongside their Siem Reap cultural itinerary.

AGS recommends Phokeethra as a strong option for lower-handicap discerning golfers visiting Siem Reap who want to experience the course where professional golf was played in Cambodia. Pairing it with Angkor Golf Resort creates an excellent two-round Siem Reap program at contrasting levels of celebrity design prestige.

curatorBriefHtml: Phokeethra Country Club (opened 2004 by Weerayudth Phetbuasak, 25 minutes west of downtown Siem Reap) is Cambodia’s original championship pioneer — former host of the Asian Tour’s Cambodian Open and famous for its iconic restored 11th-century Khmer stone bridge spanning the creek on holes 9 and 10. Measuring 6,791 yards from the Blue Tees (Par 72), the lush Paspalum layout puts water in play on nearly every hole, culminating in a thrilling island-style finishing stretch.

Having played Phokeethra personally, it delivers classic championship character and genuine historical atmosphere — a tougher, tighter water test than neighboring Angkor Golf Resort that rewards disciplined tee shots and crisp iron carries.
Managed by Sofitel, Phokeethra is the essential second championship course in Siem Reap alongside Angkor Golf Resort on our Cambodia Angkor Odyssey.

scorecard.gradeBadge: Asian Tour Cambodia Open Host • Siem Reap
scorecard.verdict: Home of the Asian Tour's Johnnie Walker Cambodian Open. Features an authentic 11th-century stone bridge on the 9th hole and delivers a classic parkland challenge amidst ancient history.

faqs.q: What is the famous Khmer landmark inside Phokeethra Country Club?
faqs.a: An authentic restored 11th-century Roluos-era Khmer stone bridge sits right between the 9th and 10th holes — offering one of the most unique historical backdrops in Asian golf.

faqs.q: How does Phokeethra Country Club compare to Angkor Golf Resort?
faqs.a: Phokeethra is a former Asian Tour host with abundant water hazards and tighter forced carries, whereas Angkor Golf Resort (Faldo) offers wider driving corridors and bolder green-side bunkering. Playing both creates the complete Siem Reap golf experience.

faqs.q: How far is Phokeethra Country Club from Siem Reap town?
faqs.a: Roughly 25 minutes west of downtown Siem Reap luxury hotels (Raffles, Jaya House, Zannier) by private touring vehicle.

faqs.q: When is the best season to play Phokeethra?
faqs.a: November through March is Siem Reap’s dry high season with sunny mornings and calm conditions.
